video.title: 5 TYPES of Websites That Can Make $5k/Month in 12 Months

summary: Spencer Haws of Niche Pursuits lists the five types of websites he would build to reach $5,000 a month within 12 months: SaaS tools, e-commerce with your own product, free tool websites monetised by ads, paid membership communities, and newsletters grown with paid ads against known revenue per subscriber. He backs each with examples (his Link Whisper and Long Tail Pro, his pillow brand sold for $425k, youtubethumbnaildownloader.com, ZeroGPT, Creator Science Lab, MarketBeat). He also says to avoid search-dependent blogs, affiliate sites and social-traffic sites because of AI, Google and platform algorithm risk. Key takeaway: build websites with utility or owned audiences rather than search-dependent content.

tactics.name: Find a SaaS idea from your own pain
steps: Notice a repetitive task that costs you hours (internal linking)
Search for existing tools; if none fit your platform (WordPress), build it
Use AI coding tools to ship an MVP

quote.text: What is a pain point that people in your niche are having? What is something that people will actually pay for
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

tactics.name: Paid newsletter growth flywheel
steps: Pick a niche with sponsorship potential
Keep cost per subscriber below revenue per subscriber and scale spend

quote.text: the goal is to optimize your ads so that it costs you less money to add a new subscriber than you make on an average subscriber
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

warnings.warning: Don't start a blog or content site reliant on Google or other organic search traffic if you want $5k/month in 12 months, unless you have an alternative traffic source or ad arbitrage.

quote.text: I cannot recommend that you start a blog or content website that is reliant on search traffic
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

warnings.warning: Affiliate sites are risky: programs can be taken away and Google dependence is fragile.

quote.text: an affiliate program can get taken away or other unforeseen challenges are more likely to occur
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

warnings.warning: Websites relying on social traffic (Pinterest, Facebook) fight platforms that keep users on-platform and face algorithm risk.

quote.text: If you're relying on Facebook, Pinterest, and other social media sites, then you face significant algorithm risk
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

warnings.warning: Revenue figures for third-party tool sites are estimates, not verified.

lessons.lesson: Focus on websites with utility (software, tools) rather than pure content in the AI search era.

quote.text: I'm really trying to get you to focus on websites that have utility
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

lessons.lesson: Know your cost per acquisition and revenue per customer; then scale as long as the gap is positive.

quote.text: When you know how much it costs to get an email subscriber and you know how much you can make off a single email subscriber on average, you can scale
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

lessons.lesson: Owning your own product beats affiliate or dropshipping for durability.
Treat Google, affiliate and social traffic as gravy, not the main source.

quote.text: These should be gravy, not the main focus
quote.speaker: Spencer Haws

lessons.lesson: AI coding tools lower the barrier to shipping a software MVP; the bottleneck is the idea.
Communities can be valuable because people crave human interaction as AI spreads.

evidence_quality.rationale: Listicle with a few first-hand claims from the author's own businesses but mostly third-party examples and traffic-based revenue estimates; Whisper transcript.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsored by Build Your Store/AutoDS; author owns Link Whisper and Niche Pursuits.

extraction.review_notes: Overall this is a solid extraction. It captures all five recommended website types, the sponsor segment, and the three types to avoid, and most claims are labelled correctly as first-hand or second-hand. The errors are small: an invented year in a warning, a mis-attributed Shopify trial cost, and a delivery automation score for the own-product e-commerce idea that was set too high. One closing metric claim ($43k/month tool site) was missed. The evidence rating of C and the promotional-conflict note are appropriate.
